task: Audit polynomial-time exact support compression for the CYCLE2 bipartite perfect-matching law.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For a finite supplied bipartite graph with equal shore sizes, m labelled actual edges, rational feasible perfect-matching marginal x, rational actual-edge feature columns A_e of Euclidean norm at most one, dyadic level T, and a deterministic exact rational Li signing routine satisfying the CYCLE2 <99 theorem, there is a deterministic polynomial-bit-time algorithm that outputs at most m+1 actual perfect matchings M_i and nonnegative rational weights lambda_i summing to one, with sum_i lambda_i 1_{M_i}=x exactly. Every output atom is retained from a feasible branch of the CYCLE2 residual-cycle/dyadic-cycle-signing tree and obeys ||A(1_{M_i}-x)||_infinity <= m*2^-T + 99*sum_{t=1}^T 2^-t U_t(P_i) for a retained branch history P_i. In particular all output atoms obey the original sampler-tree bound m*2^-T + 99*max_P sum_t 2^-t U_t(P), and the coarse unit-edge-feature bound m*2^-T+99m. The algorithm uses synchronous branching of at most m+1 current states, followed after each round/level by exact affine-dependence elimination among at most 2(m+1) existing feasible candidates.
claims.status: internally proved conditional on the CYCLE2 Li signing theorem; explicit-support implementation not yet coded or finite-tested
claims.proof_path: SUPPORT_COMPRESSION_AUDIT.md; base cycle and signing construction in CYCLE2_REPORT.md and cycle2_bipartite_sampler.py
claims.supersedes: The UNKNOWN efficient extraction status in CYCLE2_CLAIMS.json claim EXPLICIT-SUPPORT-CARATHEODORY-EXISTENCE is superseded by this constructive synchronous-compression argument; the original report remains unchanged.
claims.oracle_contract: Exact input validation by rational nonnegativity and vertex degree equations; deterministic graph cycle search/decomposition; exact rational signing calls; exact affine-dependence elimination. No optimization or separation oracle. Li signing is source-reported as polynomial-bit-time and is not independently implemented/validated here.
claims.precision_and_costs: Let L_x be total binary input length of x and Q a common denominator with log Q<=L_x. Endpoint branch denominators are <=2Q. Initial branching adds O(m^2(L_x+1)) common-weight-denominator bits. Affine-dependence coefficients at initial compression have O(m(log Q+log(m+1))) bits by determinant/Hadamard bounds; at dyadic level t they have O(m(t+log(m+1))) bits. At most m+1 eliminations occur per compression, at most m initial compressions and T dyadic compressions. A conservative final common-weight-denominator height is O(m^3(L_x+log(m+1))+m^2(T^2+T log(m+1))+T). The support construction uses polynomial bit time in (|V|,m,d,L_x,L_A,T), with at most (m+1)T Li-signing calls and output support size at most m+1. Sampling the explicit output law from common denominator D uses exact rejection with expected O(log D) fair bits and unbounded worst-case bits.
claims.falsifier: A reachable residual state with no fractional even cycle; failure of either endpoint branch to preserve feasibility or conditional mean; a dyadic plus/minus branch that is not a nonnegative integer b-matching of half degree; an affine-dependence elimination that changes total mass or edge-coordinate mean; output support larger than m+1; or a claimed weight bit bound contradicted by the stated determinant/denominator accounting.
claims.prior_art_boundary: The algorithmic compression is the standard exact affine-dependence/Caratheodory reduction applied synchronously to existing candidates; no novelty or priority claim. Primary source checks for dependent rounding and the source-reported Li signing result remain in CYCLE2_SOURCES.md. The result-113 papers are not used as evidence for this support-compression claim.
claims.next_gate: Implement the explicit-support routine and test exact marginals, matching feasibility, weight bit heights, and per-atom path certificates on small bipartite instances; independently review the Li signing primitive.
